overview: The Kamakura period marks the rise of the samurai warrior class and establishment of Japan's first military government. Zen Buddhism, martial values and austere aesthetics shaped a culture distinct from the aristocratic Heian period.

items.text: Zen Buddhism introduced from China, emphasizing meditation and discipline.
Pure Land and Nichiren Buddhism gain mass followings among common people.
Bushido ideals of loyalty, honor and courage develop.
Portrait sculpture of monks and warriors in realistic style.
Emaki narrative handscrolls depict military tales and religious stories.
Zen gardens and ink painting introduced from China.
Samurai warriors become the dominant social class.
The court in Kyoto retains ceremonial authority while Kamakura holds military power.
The shogunate system governed Japan for nearly 700 years.
Zen Buddhism profoundly influenced Japanese culture, arts and martial practices.

fall.text: The Kamakura shogunate fell to imperial loyalist forces, though military rule continued under the Ashikaga shogunate.

sources.title: Khan Academy, Introduction to the Samurai
